name: Refill drinking-water depot (DAMIU) SLHS and periodic lab-test compliance desk
buyer: Owners of refill drinking-water depots (family-run; 84,558 registered nationally as of Dec 2025)
trigger: Duties: NIB, SLHS hygiene-sanitation certificate, periodic accredited-lab water tests, licensed raw-water source letter, gallon checks. Only 4.01% have SLHS (Asdamindo); DKI Jakarta closed depots after E. coli findings (Dec 2025). Permenkes frequencies unverified.
existing: Competitor search 'aplikasi pencatatan depot air minum isi ulang SLHS uji lab software DAMIU' found no ready product, only an old 2011 academic web-based registry design. No state portal found for depot owners (SIKELIM not confirmed to exist).
unchecked: Current Permenkes text and test frequency; SLHS issuing process, fee and validity; whether any Dinkes app or lab-booking platform exists; Asdamindo membership; price tolerance of depot owners; legal basis of the Dec 2025 DKI crackdown.

first_check.duty: The duty is real and in force. Under PP 28/2025 (OSS licensing), KBLI 11052 (refill drinking water) is medium-high risk. Depots need an NIB and a standard certificate, and SLHS is a PB UMKU requirement. Permenperin 9/2021 also lists SLHS as a requirement. Kepmenperindag 651/2004 art. 6(2) requires a lab test at an accredited or government-designated lab at least once every 6 months. Hukumonline (Sept 2025) says it is still in force. Sanctions under art. 10(2) run from a verbal warning to suspension to licence revocation. The district or city Dinkes issues SLHS after a sanitarian's inspection (IKL) and a lab result no older than 1 month. Validity is 3 years in one source and 2 years in another (unverified). The test frequency in Permenkes 2/2023 is unverified: secondary sources say monthly microbiology and 6-monthly chemistry (halalmui.org) or 3-monthly (Poltekkes). Enforcement exists: Satpol PP DKI closed depots on 10-11 Dec 2025 for operating without permits and for E. coli findings.
first_check.market: 84,558 registered depots as of 25 Dec 2025 (Kemendag/Asdamindo figure, restated by JawaPos on 29 Jul 2026). Only 4.01% (about 3,390) hold SLHS. In Q1 2024 there were 78,378 depots, with 1,755 holding SLHS. Most are family-run micro businesses.
first_check.competitor: I found no commercial app that handles the SLHS and lab-test compliance job for depots. Software found is academic POS, ordering and IoT prototypes, plus an old 2011 academic design for a Semarang web registry. The state side runs through OSS (some districts, e.g. Lumajang, route SLHS via OSS) and Dinkes or Puskesmas sanitarians. Kemenkes e.satu.kemkes.go.id is used for inspection data on public facilities, not for depot owners. Labs (Labkesda and private accredited labs) are the de facto service providers. Asdamindo runs training and courses with Kemenkes and Kemenperin.
first_check.reason: The duties are real: NIB/OSS, an SLHS from Dinkes, and lab tests at least every 6 months. There are about 84.5k depots, compliance is only about 4%, and contamination is widespread, so policy pressure is rising. JawaPos (29 Jul 2026) reports Kemendag highlighting the low compliance. I found no software competitor. But the core job is a physical sample, a lab test and a sanitarian inspection, so software adds little. Owners are price-sensitive micro businesses, and enforcement is sporadic and local, as with the DKI Dec 2025 closures. The lab-test frequency in Permenkes 2/2023 is unverified. The more workable model is a done-for-you service (sample pickup, lab booking, SLHS file via OSS/Dinkes) with lab revenue share and distribution through Asdamindo. That model is local and operations-heavy, not a simple SaaS product.

challenge_check.killer: No full killer found. Partial competitors: izin.co.id's paid SLHS processing service (one-off, no tracking of recurring tests); SLHS applications through OSS/DPMPTSP in some districts (e.g. Lumajang); sanitarians from Puskesmas and Dinkes; cheap Labkesda tests where some labs (e.g. Perumda Tirta Kanjuruhan) send staff to take samples.
challenge_check.reason: Survives, but only just. I found no software that tracks SLHS and recurring lab tests for depot owners. Asdamindo has no app. In Lumajang, SLHS applications go through OSS, but OSS only takes the application and does not track tests. The duty is real and enforced. Kemendag restated six obligations in July 2026. Satpol PP DKI closed 18 depots on 1–5 October 2026, and only 0.9% of Jakarta's 2,541 depots hold SLHS. The weak points: izin.co.id already sells done-for-you SLHS processing. A summary on halalmui.org says monthly microbiology tests are required, but a Hukumonline piece citing older rules says every 6 months, and I did not read the Permenkes text myself. A Labkesda microbiology test costs about Rp40k, so a reminder tool is worth little. The real barrier is the cost of sanitation upgrades, and family-run depots are unlikely to pay much.
